documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: HPI:
91 y/o male with known COPD presents to ED at 01:20 with 3 days of worsening dyspnea, cough, and thick yellow sputum.
Symptoms began after a head cold in the household; grandson had URI last week.
Pt reports he could not walk to the bathroom without stopping to rest; sleeps in recliner x 2 nights.
No fever at home. No chest pain. No hemoptysis. No leg swelling.
Uses home albuterol MDI q4h prn, has been using it every 2h for 2 days with little relief.
On home O2 2L NC at night only; wore it continuously the last 24h.
ED course: SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.36, PaCO2 47, PaO2 66 on 2L.
Alert and fully oriented throughout ED stay, answering all questions appropriately.
Past Medical History:
COPD, GOLD stage III per prior PFTs, FEV1 approx 42% predicted
Former smoker, 60 pack-years, quit at age 74
Hypertension
BPH
Osteoarthritis, both knees
Chronic kidney disease stage 3a, baseline creatinine 1.3
Prior COPD admission 8 months ago, treated with steroids and abx, no intubation
Home Medications:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 650 mg q8h prn knee pain
Allergies: penicillin - rash
Social: lives with daughter, uses rollator, independent for ADLs with setup. No alcohol. No tobacco x 17 yrs.
Family Hx: noncontributory.
ROS: positive for dyspnea, cough, sputum, poor appetite. Denies dysuria, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, headache.
Physical Exam:
Vitals 03:40: T 37.1, HR 104, BP 148/78, RR 32, SpO2 90% on 4L NC
General: thin elderly male, in obvious respiratory distress, sitting upright at edge of bed
Resp: Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, poor air movement at bases
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no JVD
Abd: soft, nontender, nondistended, bowel sounds present
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness, warm
Neuro: grossly intact, follows all commands, moves all extremities
Skin: intact, no rash
Labs:
WBC 13.2, Hgb 12.8, Plt 244
Na 138, K 4.2, Cl 99, HCO3 28, BUN 26, Cr 1.34, glucose 156
Lactate 1.6. Resp viral panel sent.
Imaging:
CXR portable: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation, no effusion
Assessment/Plan:
91 y/o male with severe COPD, acute exacerbation likely viral triggered, with hypoxemia and mild hypercapnia.
1. COPD exacerbation - admit to stepdown. Continue albuterol-ipratropium neb q4h scheduled, q2h prn.
2. steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours.
3. Azithromycin 500 mg IV day 1 then 250 mg daily given penicillin allergy.
4. O2 to keep SpO2 88-92%, titrate NC. Repeat ABG if RR or work of breathing worsens.
5. Monitor CBG q6h given steroid burden.
6. HTN - hold amlodipine if SBP < 110, otherwise continue.
7. VTE ppx enoxaparin 30 mg SC daily for CrCl.
8. PT/OT consult when less dyspneic. Discussed plan with pt and daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: Subjective:
Pt reports breathing somewhat easier than on arrival. Cough productive, sputum lighter in color.
Still short of breath with any movement in bed. Slept in upright position. No chest pain.
Alert, conversant, oriented x3, answering in full sentences this morning.
Overnight: 2 prn nebs at 23:10 and 04:30 for wheeze.
Vitals:
Intake 900 mL, output 1150 mL
Exam:
Resp: expiratory wheeze still present but improved air movement, no accessory muscle use at rest now
Cardiac: regular rate, no murmur
Abd: soft, nontender. Ext: no edema
Labs 05:40:
WBC 11.4, Hgb 12.5, Plt 238
CBG 06:00 was 288; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
Resp viral panel: rhinovirus positive
Assessment/Plan:
1. COPD exacerbation, improving. Continue albuterol-ipratropium q4h and prn.
2. steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours - continue today, plan taper to oral prednisone HD3-4.
3. Steroid hyperglycemia - insulin sliding scale q6h, add correction with meals, avoid dextrose fluids.
4. Wean O2 to lowest FiO2 for SpO2 88-92%.
5. Azithromycin day 2 of 5.
6. Mobilize to chair with PT today.
7. Continue enoxaparin ppx.
Discussed with RN; RT to reassess after 10:00 neb.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5
lines: Subjective:
Pt walked 40 feet in hallway with rollator and PT yesterday afternoon, SpO2 nadir 89% on 2L.
Reports breathing near his usual baseline. Cough now dry and infrequent. Appetite returning, ate most of breakfast.
No dyspnea at rest. Denies chest pain, no dizziness.
Vitals:
T 36.8, HR 82, BP 132/70, RR 18, SpO2 93% on 2L NC, 90% on room air at rest
Exam:
General: comfortable, sitting up in chair, oriented and engaged
Resp: mild scattered expiratory wheeze at bases, good air movement, no accessory muscle use
Cardiac: regular. Abd: soft. Ext: no edema.
Labs:
CBG trend last 24h: 212, 188, 174, 161
BMP: Na 140, K 3.9, HCO3 26, BUN 22, Cr 1.24
Assessment/Plan:
1. COPD exacerbation - much improved. Nebs spaced to q6h, prn in between.
2. Steroid taper - on prednisone 40 mg PO daily, day 2 of oral; plan total 5 days oral then stop.
3. Steroid hyperglycemia improving with taper - continue sliding scale, reduce to q8h, likely off at discharge.
4. Azithromycin completed 5 days.
5. Resume home tiotropium and budesonide-formoterol today; RT to re-teach inhaler technique with spacer.
6. O2: trial off during ambulation today, home O2 nocturnal as before.
7. PT to continue; daughter available for home support.
8. Anticipate discharge HD6 if stable off continuous O2 and ambulating.
Family updated by phone at 11:15.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
lines: Discharge diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of COPD, rhinovirus-associated, with hypoxemic respiratory distress.
Secondary: steroid-induced hyperglycemia, hypertension, CKD stage 3a, BPH.
Length of stay: HD1 to HD6.
Hospital Course:
91 y/o male with severe COPD presented at 01:20 with 3 days of progressive dyspnea and purulent sputum after a household URI.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
On exam there was visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.36, PaCO2 47, PaO2 66 on 2L.
Admitted to stepdown on scheduled nebs, azithromycin for penicillin allergy, and O2 titrated to SpO2 88-92%.
steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
Work of breathing improved by HD2 with RR 24 on 3L. Wheeze largely resolved by HD4.
Steroids transitioned to oral prednisone HD4. Glucose trended down to 161 by HD5 and sliding scale discontinued HD6.
Azithromycin completed 5 days. CXR showed hyperinflation without consolidation; no repeat imaging needed.
Ambulated 120 feet with rollator on HD6, SpO2 90% on room air at rest and 89% with exertion.
Discharge Vitals: T 36.7, HR 78, BP 128/72, RR 18, SpO2 92% on room air at rest.
Discharge Exam: comfortable, alert and oriented, speaking full sentences, no accessory muscle use, faint end-expiratory wheeze.
Discharge Medications:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 2 more days then stop
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID, rinse mouth after use
Albuterol MDI with spacer 2 puffs q4h prn
Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 650 mg q8h prn
Home O2 2L NC nightly as before admission.
Follow-up:
Primary care in 5 to 7 days for repeat exam and finger-stick glucose check.
Pulmonary clinic in 4 weeks with spirometry.
Home PT referral placed; daughter to assist with ADLs.
Instructions: use spacer with every MDI dose, call for increased sputum, fever, or need for rescue inhaler more than q4h.
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination status reviewed; influenza vaccine given prior to discharge.
Discharged HD6 at 14:40 to home with daughter, stable.
